The Pochaev Icon of the Mother of God

Icons

Theotokos

The Pochaev Icon of the Mother of God

Our Lady of Pochaev · Pochayiv

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 1:49–50

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Pochaev icon is associated with the Dormition monastery in southwest Ukraine. Father Alexander Golubov’s historical account distinguishes written evidence about the monastery and the icon’s donation from local traditions concerning earlier apparitions.

[1] Opening description; early history and endowment

What is depicted

Golubov describes Mary holding Christ on her right arm and a cloth covering his feet. The child blesses; seven smaller saints appear along the sides and bottom. The displayed image shows the decorated shrine around this particular Mother-and-Child composition.

[1] Opening paragraph: description of the icon

History and tradition

His account connects the icon with Metropolitan Neophyte’s visit in 1559 and his gift to Anna Goiskaya. Anna’s 1597 endowment transferred the icon to the monastery. A distinct local tradition places an apparition and footprint at Mount Pochaev around 1340.

[1] Metropolitan Neophyte; Anna Goiskaya; footprint tradition

Published explanation

The OCA’s July 23 commemoration concerns deliverance from the siege of 1675. Its narrative describes the Mother of God and Saint Job appearing above the monastery. It also identifies monastery books as records of reported healings and other miracles.

[2] Feast explanation; siege account; monastery records

For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name. And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation.

[3] Luke 1:49–50
